title: The store opens once at boot and is ready when the entry point returns
asA: operator whose deploy needs a persistence surface ready before the first request is served
iWant: the store to be opened exactly once at boot through a single entry point that runs migrations before returning
soThat: the application starts in a known persistence state and no request runs against a half-initialised store

acceptanceCriteria.description: The application exposes a single named function or module export that opens the store, and the process invokes it exactly once during boot before any request handler binds.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the store event log contains exactly one opened event whose timestamp precedes the timestamp of the first served request

acceptanceCriteria.description: The store opens with a path or connection string sourced from application configuration; no consumer code hard-codes the store location.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the application is configured with a store path or connection string
acceptanceCriteria.when: the boot sequence runs the open entry point
acceptanceCriteria.then: the store event log's opened event carries the same store identifier the configuration supplied, and a grep of the source tree finds the identifier resolved from configuration rather than hard-coded

acceptanceCriteria.description: The open entry point returns only after migrations have run to the build's max known schema version; consumer code that runs after the entry point returns sees a schema at that version.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the boot sequence has invoked the open entry point and control has returned
acceptanceCriteria.when: consumer code queries the schema version via the store facade
acceptanceCriteria.then: the reported version equals the build's max known migration version

acceptanceCriteria.description: Permission denied on the store file refuses open. Given the configured store file path resides in a directory the process user cannot read or write (chmod 000, or a file owned by a different uid without read permission), when the store facade opens, then the underlying engine surfaces a SQLITE_CANTOPEN-family error and the facade re-throws a named storePermissionDenied error carrying the resolved path (never carrying any credential material or file contents), and no opened event fires on the sink.
acceptanceCriteria.given: store file path unreadable or unwritable by the process user
acceptanceCriteria.then: the underlying engine surfaces SQLITE_CANTOPEN; the facade re-throws storePermissionDenied naming the resolved path; no opened event fires

acceptanceCriteria.description: Concurrent WAL writer against the same store file. Given two processes both opening the same SQLite file in WAL mode against the same on-disk artifact, when both invoke a write verb concurrently, then the SQLite WAL semantics serialise the writes (one commits, the other retries the transaction via the busy handler up to the configured busy timeout) and no writer is silently dropped; a busy-timeout exhaustion surfaces as a storeBusy error carrying the elapsed wait, and neither writer observes partial state from the other.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two processes opening the same on-disk store file in WAL mode with concurrent write verbs
acceptanceCriteria.then: WAL serialises the writes via the busy handler; a busy-timeout exhaustion surfaces storeBusy naming the elapsed wait; no writer observes partial cross-process state
